title: Bond
lede: All 25 official Bond films, best first, plus the unofficial two. Tap Year for release order. Craig's five are one continuous story, so watch those in order.

levels.name: Joint first
levels.note: Lazenby's one shot, Goldfinger and the Orient Express.

levels.name: Very good
levels.note: Skyfall, the ski jump, Dr. No, Dalton twice, a 2CV and the sharks.

levels.name: Good fun
levels.note: Craig's farewell, a volcano, crocodiles, a car park and a clown suit.

levels.name: Patchy
levels.note: Spectre, Vegas, a nuclear physicist, space and a slide whistle.

levels.name: The dregs
levels.note: Quantum, Moore at 57 and the invisible car.

levels.name: Better spies and rip-offs
levels.note: The anti-Bonds, the knock-offs and the piss-takes.

core.b: George Lazenby's only outing: Blofeld's Alpine clinic, a ski chase, Diana Rigg, and the ending that makes Bond human. Joint first.
The template: the gold-painted girl, Oddjob's hat, the Aston Martin, 'No, Mr Bond, I expect you to die!' Joint first.
Connery's best as an actual spy film: Istanbul, a Lektor decoder, and Robert Shaw on the Orient Express. Joint first.
Brosnan's debut: the bungee jump, a tank through St Petersburg, Sean Bean, and Famke Janssen crushing men with her thighs.
Craig's reboot: parkour in Madagascar, poker in Montenegro, Eva Green, and the rope chair. Start of a five-film story. Also on Action.

br.note: The unofficial spoof: Niven, Sellers, Woody Allen and chaos

core.b: Mendes and Deakins: Javier Bardem's blond villain, Shanghai neon, and a siege at Bond's childhood home.
Moore's best: the Union Jack parachute ski jump, the Lotus submarine, and Jaws.
Where it began: 'Bond. James Bond.' Ursula Andress from the sea, and Jamaica.
Dalton's first: a cello case down a mountain, Afghanistan, and a properly cold Bond.
Moore brought down to earth: a Greek mountain climb, a 2CV chase, crossbows.
Underwater battles, a jetpack, the Bahamas and Largo's sharks.

br.note: The unofficial Thunderball remake: Connery's return at 52, Klaus Maria Brandauer, a video-game duel

core.b: Dalton goes rogue for revenge: drug lords, a tanker chase, a man fed to a shark. Nastier than any Bond before it.
Craig's finale, and the end of his serial. The Norwegian house, the Italian chase, and that ending.
The volcano lair, Blofeld's face at last, and Roald Dahl's script. Dodgy 'turning Japanese' bit.
Moore's debut: crocodile-hopping, voodoo, the McCartney theme. Dated in every sense.
Jonathan Pryce's media mogul, Michelle Yeoh, and a remote-control BMW in a car park.
Moore in a clown suit defusing a bomb, and Tarzan yells in the jungle. Fun, daft.
The Day of the Dead opening is superb; then Blofeld turns out to be Bond's foster brother.
Connery back for the money, Las Vegas, and Mr Wint and Mr Kidd.
Sophie Marceau's villain is good. Denise Richards as a nuclear physicist is not.
Bond in space, with laser guns. Jaws gets a girlfriend.

core.t: The Man with the Golden Gun
core.b: Christopher Lee is great; the slide-whistle car jump is not.
Written during a strike and edited in a blender. Bolivian water rights. It's short.
Moore at 57, Grace Jones and Christopher Walken. Duran Duran's theme is the best bit.
Invisible car, CGI surfing, Madonna. The franchise jumped the shark, then rebooted.

beyond.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
beyond.b: Le Carré's answer to Bond: Richard Burton's burnt-out agent sent on one last grubby mission across the Berlin Wall. Black and white, bleak, brilliant. Also on Thriller.
Michael Caine's Harry Palmer: glasses, a council flat, filing, and cooking omelettes. Made by Bond's producer as the anti-Bond. On the BFI 100.
James Coburn's Derek Flint: a lighter with 82 functions, four girlfriends and karate. The best of the 60s knock-offs.
Jean Dujardin's suave, staggeringly ignorant French agent in 1955 Egypt. A perfect Connery parody from the team behind The Artist.

beyond.t: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery
beyond.b: Mike Myers' frozen 60s spy and Dr. Evil's one million dollars. Yeah, baby.

seq.t: Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me

beyond.b: Colin Firth's tailor-spy and a church massacre to Free Bird. Bond with a Savile Row suit and no restraint. Also on Action and Superheroes.
